guide.title: Mendelssohn: String Quartet No. 2, Op. 13 – I. Adagio: A Listening Guide
guide.overview: This movement has three parts, and its home key is A minor. A slow opening (Part 1) leads into a fast middle (Section 2, Allegro vivace). Then comes a return marked "a tempo" (Section 3). The score is in good shape, but keys and chords here are estimated by computer. Listen for Violin 1 at the very start, the change of pace at [m. 19], and the loudest point near [m. 197], as estimated by computer.

listening_points.headline: Violin 1 leads the opening
listening_points.text: Violin 1 leads at the start [m. 0-3]. The other instruments move together with it in block-like harmony. The key is A major, and the volume starts at mf and settles to p. A marked swell (crescendo) appears in [m. 3].

listening_points.headline: A darker, hushed turn to F# minor
listening_points.text: The key estimate moves to F# minor, which sounds more shadowy [m. 5-10]. The music gets very soft (pp) at [m. 6]. A marked swell appears at [m. 7], and a marked fade at [m. 9]. Violin 1 probably leads, with low confidence in places.

listening_points.headline: Brightening back to A major, then louder
listening_points.text: The key returns to A major [m. 11-13]. The volume rises to f at [m. 12], with a marked swell. It then settles to mf at [m. 13].

listening_points.headline: Fading in E major, ending the slow opening
listening_points.text: The key moves to E major [m. 14]. The lines become independent, each part going its own way. The music grows soft (p at [m. 16], pp at [m. 17]). At [m. 17] the parts play in unison or octaves, meaning the same notes at different heights. A swell is marked at [m. 18].

listening_points.headline: Allegro vivace begins; the mood turns to A minor
listening_points.text: The fast section starts at [m. 19]. A trio texture appears at [m. 20]: only three of the four parts play. The key estimate turns to A minor at [m. 22], which darkens the mood. Violin 1 probably leads at [m. 23].

listening_points.headline: The lead passes around the quartet
listening_points.text: The lead passes from Viola [m. 24] to Violin 2 [m. 25] to Cello [m. 26]. Violin 1 then takes over [m. 27-30], and the volume drops to p. The others accompany. Listen for the changing voices.

listening_points.headline: E minor and a louder, driving stretch
listening_points.text: The key estimate moves to E minor at [m. 44] and stays there for a long time. The volume rises to f at [m. 45]. At [m. 52] the music reaches ff. Violin 1 probably leads much of this.

listening_points.headline: Quiet again, with Violin 1 clearly in front
listening_points.text: After a fade marked at [m. 57], the volume is p at [m. 58]. It drops to pp at [m. 65]. Violin 1 carries the lead with high confidence [m. 59-62].

listening_points.headline: A lone violin in E major
listening_points.text: The key brightens to E major at [m. 89]. At [m. 91] the texture is solo: Violin 1 plays alone, very softly (pp). Then the lines become independent again at [m. 93].

listening_points.headline: A loud, restless stretch through changing keys
listening_points.text: The music reaches ff at [m. 98]. Violin 1 leads [m. 98-102]. The estimated key shifts quickly: B minor [m. 99], F# minor [m. 102], then D major [m. 105].

listening_points.headline: A hushed, uncertain passage
listening_points.text: The key estimate moves to G minor, and the volume falls to pp at [m. 108]. It then moves to A minor [m. 111], with p. A swell is marked at [m. 114]. The lead is unclear here, because confidence is low.

listening_points.headline: Loud, then fading toward the return
listening_points.text: After a loud stretch at ff [m. 124], the volume drops suddenly to p at [m. 128], and a fade is also marked there. The music settles in A minor at [m. 130], and reaches pp at [m. 137].

listening_points.headline: The "a tempo" section begins
listening_points.text: Section 3 starts at [m. 141] and is marked a tempo, which means back to the earlier speed. Violin 1 leads at [m. 142] with p. A crescendo at [m. 149] then leads to ff at [m. 150], and a marked fade follows at [m. 151].

listening_points.headline: Very loud, then a hush in E major
listening_points.text: The music is ff at [m. 164], with Violin 1 leading clearly. It softens to f at [m. 168] and then to p at [m. 171]. A short brightening to E major comes at [m. 171-173].

listening_points.headline: The loudest moment (a computer estimate)
listening_points.text: The music is ff at [m. 189], then suddenly p at [m. 190]. It returns to f at [m. 194] and ff at [m. 196]. A computer estimate marks [m. 197] as the loudest and busiest point. The lines there are independent.

listening_points.headline: Wandering keys, then home to A minor
listening_points.text: The estimated key moves to B minor [m. 208], then D minor [m. 212], then F major [m. 221]. Violin 1 plays solo at [m. 210] and [m. 213]. The music is very soft (pp) from [m. 218]. A minor returns at [m. 224].

listening_points.headline: A soft stretch, then a loud ending
listening_points.text: The music is ff at [m. 238], then falls to p at [m. 244]. A swell is marked at [m. 245-246]. At [m. 248] it is ff again, and Violin 1 leads. It ends in A minor with all parts together (homophonic) at [m. 251].

glossary.explanation: All parts move together in the same rhythm, like a hymn. One part is the tune and the others make chords under it.
One part has the tune. The others play support underneath.
Each part plays its own tune-like line at the same time.
Parts play the same notes, either at the same height or an octave apart.
The home note and scale that a passage feels based on. Major keys sound brighter. Minor keys sound darker.
Loudness marks: pp is very soft, p soft, mf medium loud, f loud, ff very loud.
